subject: History
description: First War of Independence — causes, key figures, aftermath

questions.stem: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at:
questions.explanation: Sepoys of the 3rd Bengal Light Cavalry at Meerut cantonment mutinied on 10 May 1857 over the greased-cartridge controversy. The next day they reached Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar II as Emperor. Mangal Pandey's earlier action at Barrackpore (29 March 1857) is often called a precursor, not the revolt itself.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: MANGAL PANDEY, who famously challenged the British on 29 March 1857, belonged to which regiment?
questions.explanation: Mangal Pandey — 34th BNI, Barrackpore (near Calcutta). Attacked British officers Lt. Baugh and Gen. Hearsey over the greased-cartridge controversy. Court-martialled and hanged on 8 April 1857. Often considered the 'first martyr' of the 1857 uprising.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the LEADER with the CENTRE of revolt. A. Rani Lakshmibai.  B. Tatya Tope.  C. Nana Saheb.  D. Begum Hazrat Mahal. List-II: 1. Jhansi.  2. Gwalior / Kanpur.  3. Kanpur (Bithur).  4. Lucknow.
questions.explanation: Lakshmibai — Jhansi (MP); died 17 June 1858 near Gwalior. Tatya Tope — Nana Saheb's general; his guerrilla campaign around Gwalior and central India. Nana Saheb (Dhondu Pant) — Kanpur (Bithur was his seat). Begum Hazrat Mahal — Lucknow (wife of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The immediate cause of the 1857 Revolt was:

options.option_text: Introduction of the new Enfield rifle cartridges

questions.explanation: Enfield P53 rifle used greased cartridges rumoured to contain COW + PIG fat — religiously offensive to both Hindu and Muslim sepoys who had to bite off the ends. This lit the spark; wider causes were political (Doctrine of Lapse, annexations), economic (ryotwari exploitation, destruction of Indian manufacturing), religious, and military grievances. greased with animal fat.

questions.stem: The 'DOCTRINE OF LAPSE' — annexing princely states without heirs — was associated with:
questions.explanation: Dalhousie — annexed Satara (1848), Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Baghat, Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854), and finally Awadh in 1856 (on grounds of misgovernance, not lapse). These annexations fuelled the revolt. Lord Canning was Governor-General at the time of 1857 revolt.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: After the 1857 Revolt, administration of India was TRANSFERRED from the East India Company to the:
questions.explanation: Government of India Act 1858 — abolished rule of the EIC; India brought under direct British Crown rule. Governor-General was also Viceroy of the Queen. Queen Victoria's 1858 Proclamation — promised non-interference in religious affairs, equal opportunity, sanctity of adoptions etc. (mostly honoured in form, not always in substance). direct rule under the Crown.
questions.subject: History

_fixes.was: British Parliament (direct rule under the Crown)

questions.stem: V. D. Savarkar called the Revolt of 1857:
questions.explanation: V. D. Savarkar — in his 1909 book 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' (banned by the British) — called it India's First War of Independence. British historians largely called it 'the Sepoy Mutiny' or 'Indian Mutiny'. R.C. Majumdar later argued it was neither a pan-Indian war nor purely a mutiny — a mix.
